one_line: A master Malabar shipbuilder on the Chaliyar river, guardian of the Beypore uru tradition.

appearance.age_look: mid-40s, lean but strong, wiry craftsman’s build with calloused hands and steady posture
appearance.face: oval face, medium brown Malabar complexion, sun-lined skin, straight nose, trimmed moustache, thoughtful eyes with a calm, calculating gaze, default expression a focused half-smile as if assessing a hull curve
appearance.hair: thick black hair with a few strands of grey, combed back and tied into a short low knot at the nape; simple off-white cotton headband wrapped once around the forehead and knotted at the back, hairline visible
appearance.costume: era-accurate working shipwright outfit: a knee-length off-white cotton mundu (wrap skirt) with a thin maroon border, worn slightly hitched for movement; above, a plain light beige long-sleeved cotton angarkha-style tunic that overlaps at the chest and ties at the right side, sleeves rolled neatly to mid-forearm; a dark brown leather waist belt holding small wooden measuring pegs; bare feet for grip on planks, with simple dark wooden prayer beads wrapped twice around his left wrist; no fantasy armour, just practical, modest craftsman’s attire that sits correctly for medieval-to-early-modern Malabar.
appearance.signature: a long, slightly curved wooden shipwright’s batten held in his right hand, about as tall as his shoulder, used to fair hull lines, with a smooth dark-brown oiled surface and a small notch near one end; tucked into his belt at the back is a slim wooden mallet and a short iron chisel, but the batten is always the clear signature tool.

ref_desc: A mid-40s Beypore shipwright with medium brown skin, tied-back black hair and headband, in off-white mundu with maroon border and beige angarkha tunic, carrying a dark-brown wooden batten, with a brown leather belt and wooden wrist beads in a warm earthy palette.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of a mid-40s Beypore shipwright on the Malabar coast: lean but strong, medium brown sun-lined face with a thoughtful focused gaze, straight nose and trimmed moustache; thick black hair with a touch of grey combed back and tied into a short low knot, wrapped with a simple off-white headband. He wears an off-white knee-length cotton mundu with a thin maroon border, slightly hitched for ease of movement, and a plain light beige long-sleeved angarkha-style tunic overlapping and tied on the right, sleeves rolled to mid-forearm. A dark brown leather belt at the waist holds small wooden measuring pegs, and simple dark wooden prayer beads wrap his left wrist; he stands barefoot for grip on planks. His signature tool is a long, slightly curved dark-brown wooden batten used to fair hull lines, held confidently in his right hand, with a slim wooden mallet and short iron chisel tucked at the back of his belt. Use a warm earthy palette of off-white, beige, maroon, dark brown and medium brown skin, and show him from front, side and back to capture hair, garments, belt details and batten clearly.
